newsDocuments.headline: UN official urges Iran, US to let fertilizers through Hormuz Strait

segments.text: ANTALYA, (Turkey): Iran and the United States should “immediately” allow fertiliser shipments through the Strait of Hormuz to ease the crisis in some of the most vulnerable countries, a senior UN official said Saturday.
Before the conflict, a third of the world’s fertilisers passed through the Strait of Hormuz, and since the blockades, their prices had risen by 30 percent, he said.

newsDocuments.headline: US diesel below $6 a gallon at 2-month low on easing tensions, weaker demand

segments.text: NEW YORK: US diesel prices fell below $6 a gallon on average on Saturday after two months above that threshold, retreating from record highs as easing geopolitical ​tensions and seasonal demand weakness reduce pressure on fuel markets.
Diesel had surged ‌as the US-Israeli war against Iran disrupted oil supplies and Ukraine’s systematic attacks on Russian refineries stymied production.

Elevated diesel prices, a key driver of transportation and freight costs, have boosted overall inflation, causing ​pain for consumers, farmers and businesses. High fuel costs were a major ​factor helping Democrats sweep both houses of Congr

newsDocuments.headline: Oil prices set for second straight weekly drop on signs of growing supply surplus

segments.text: HOUSTON: Oil weakened on Friday, set for a second straight weekly decline, as the market weighed signs of a growing global supply surplus and Washington’s focus on blockading Iran while ramping up other economic pressures in the nine-month
Brent futures settled at USD95.84 a barrel, up 2 cents, or 0.02 percent. US West Texas Intermediate futures finished at USD88.56 a barrel, down 18 cents, or 0.20 percent.

With lower geopolitical risk from the US-Israeli war against Iran and the release on Friday of an International Energy Agency report pointing to a rise in the global oil surplus, the market is going through a major shift.

newsDocuments.headline: World oil market is returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover

segments.text: LONDON: The world oil market will return to a surplus in the fourth quarter of this year, the International Energy Agency said on Friday, as Middle East exports recover faster than global oil demand despite continued attacks on shipping.

The agency also gave more details of remaining volumes to come from a record release of oil from its members’ emergency reserves pledged in March, saying 71 million barrels would be made available by the end of February including 15 million

Oil supply will average 105 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, the Paris-based agency which advises industrialised countries, said in a monthly report, 1.7 million bpd higher than forecast demand.
